A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLANeXt study. Their text, tables, diagrams, and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete for comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original LIBERO/LIBERO-plus ablations and benchmark results, real-world robot trials in Tables 1–4, and qualitative demonstrations in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation and robot results and adds component ablations across benchmark suites and the real-world clean-table task in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The core VLANeXt recipe remains intact. The final-model configuration changes diffusion depth from 19 to 29 and frequency-loss weight from 0.1 to 0.5 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 7), constituting limited architecture and objective revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the four LIBERO and LIBERO-plus suites, DROID pretraining, and the same four Franka/Aloha manipulation tasks. The new appendix ablations reuse this existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds pi0.5 to the LIBERO comparison in Table 2, reporting a 96.9% average. Existing comparators remain, including the unchanged comparator sets for LIBERO-plus and real-world evaluations.

E3.justification: The reported final-model depth and auxiliary-loss coefficient change in the hyperparameter table. New real-world ablations in Table 6 report counts out of 10, while the main comparison retains 20 trials. The 10,000-step, batch-256 simulation training protocol remains; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the spatial-centered component study: Table 5 adds Object, Goal, and Long ablation results for soft coupling, multiple views, proprioception, and frequency loss. Table 6 adds real-world clean-table removal tests for action chunking, multiple views, soft coupling, and proprioception. These directly examine recipe generality beyond v1's primary ablation setting.

E5.justification: Both versions report success rates or success counts without seed information, repeated-training-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional evaluation episode counts do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces VLANeXt's LIBERO-plus results: the overall average changes from 80.1% to 83.9%, while background performance changes from 91.8% to 82.5%. Model settings also change, preventing an unchanged-setting gain interpretation. Table 1 revises several entries, Table 2 changes LIBERO Long from 94.6% to 94.8%, and Tables 5–6 add component results. Table 4 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theorems or proofs. The revised frequency-loss discussion supplies implementation and explanatory prose without adding a formal derivation, assumption framework, or mathematical guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the real-world claim from strong generalization to strong performance. The introduction newly claims more than 500 distinct experiments. The central three-dimensional study, 12 findings, practical recipe, and benchmark superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the Gaussian/multimodal-distribution rationale for flow matching with an asserted eventual advantage in precise control. It explains frequency-loss benefits as avoiding overfitting to trajectory jitter instead of exploiting low-rank structure. Appendix A.2 additionally interprets the extended ablations as evidence of recipe robustness.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents cross-attention conditioning, adaLN timestep conditioning, and preferential weighting of low-frequency DCT components. It supplies the main code repository address and reports code release instead of promising a future release. These are documentation and access-information improvements; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work appendix adds background on gripper, dexterous, and dynamic grasping and nonprehensile manipulation, with references including GraspNet-1Billion, MotionGrasp, and DyWA. Section 2.1 adds Peebles and Xie for conditioning details. The overarching positioning as a unified VLA design-space study remains.

P1.justification: V2 selectively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and related-work discussion. It adds Appendix A.2, folds the former settings appendix into A.3, renumbers related work from C to B, and updates publication and acknowledgement text. The main narrative structure remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds two ablation tables and retains the former hyperparameter table as Table 7. Figures 5–7 clarify action versus proprioception labels, and Figure 7 moves to the right column with associated text reflow. Table 2 gains a comparator row; the qualitative image sequences in Figures 9–11 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Tables 5–6 provide direct support for recipe generality beyond v1's spatial ablations, while clearer conditioning, loss, and code-access documentation improves reproducibility. The gains are qualified: uncertainty reporting remains absent, and v2's new claim that flow matching eventually surpasses regression lacks a corresponding reported comparison. The added validation supports a modest net improvement independently of the higher revised benchmark scores.
